transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

My mind keeps swinging between being full of plans and then feeling so foggy that I can’t focus long enough to finish anything. It's just been really hard to make any consistent progress with my work lately.

During those times when you feel full of plans, have you ever had periods where you felt so energetic or wired that you didn't need much sleep and felt like you could accomplish anything, lasting for several days at a time?

Yes, during those weeks I feel incredibly wired and will stay up almost all night redesigning my website because my mind is racing with ideas. I get so energized that I don't feel like I need much sleep, and I honestly feel convinced that I'm going to revolutionize art therapy in this city.
During those periods of high energy, have you ever experienced things that others couldn't see or hear, or felt so powerful that you believed you had special abilities or were being followed?

No, I've never seen or heard things that aren't there, and I don't feel like I'm being followed. But I do get incredibly overconfident during those high phases—while I don't think I have supernatural powers, I'll genuinely believe I'm going to completely revolutionize art therapy in my city and talk like I've already built a huge practice when I've only run a couple of workshops.

During these periods of high energy and grand ideas, have you ever needed to be hospitalized, or did these episodes cause such significant problems at work or in your relationships that you were unable to function normally?

No, I've never been hospitalized, but these ups and downs have caused really major disruptions in my life. I've missed key grant deadlines, backed out of consulting work at the last minute, and strained my marriage and friendships to the point where people are hesitant to rely on me.
During those high-energy periods, are you able to continue working and socializing, or does your behavior become so extreme that it is clearly different from your usual self to those around you?

Yes, it's definitely very different from my usual self, and my husband and friends notice it immediately. My husband says I talk in a nonstop stream so fast he can't get a word in, and I'll snap at him over tiny things like how he loads the dishwasher. While I start out feeling highly social and ambitious, it eventually turns chaotic, and people now find me too unpredictable to rely on.
During these high-energy episodes, has your behavior ever become so extreme that you were unable to work or socialize, or did you require hospitalization to prevent harm to yourself or others?

No, I have never been hospitalized, but the ups and downs have definitely disrupted my ability to work and socialize. I've missed key grant deadlines, backed out of consulting commitments at the last minute, and let my friendships and community art group slide. It's gotten to the point where people are really hesitant to rely on me anymore.
During these high-energy periods, have these episodes ever lasted for at least one full week, or were they shorter in duration?

Yes, those high-energy phases definitely last for at least a week, sometimes stretching on for a few weeks at a time. They aren't just quick bursts of energy for a day or two, but sustained periods where I am constantly revved up and making big plans. This intense state usually goes on for weeks before I eventually slide into the low, foggy phases.

During these high-energy episodes, have you ever experienced a degree of impairment that was so severe it necessitated hospitalization, or were you always able to maintain some level of functioning despite the disruptions?

No, I've never been hospitalized and have always managed to stay out of the hospital, but the disruptions are still incredibly severe. I've missed key grant deadlines, backed out of consulting commitments at the last minute, and let my friendships and community art projects slide so much that people don't feel they can rely on me anymore.

During these high-energy episodes, have you ever felt that your functioning was so impaired that you were completely unable to carry out your work or social responsibilities, even if you did not require hospitalization?

Yes, my ability to function has been severely impacted because during those high phases I take on way too many projects and then completely fail to follow through. I've missed critical grant deadlines, backed out of consulting work at the last minute, and let my community art group and friendships slide. It has gotten to the point where people in my life simply can't rely on me anymore.
